pipeline_test_failure_analyzer.overview: Diagnose JUnit / Surefire test failures and propose targeted fixes. All output is plain text for a Jenkins console — no ANSI, no markdown tables.

step.title: Read the failure input
step.description: The user will provide one of: raw console log, Surefire XML report, or a paste of the failing test output. Extract every failing test's class name, method name, exception type, and message.

step.title: Read relevant source files
step.description: For each failing test class, read: - The test file under order-service/src/test/ - The production class under order-service/src/main/ that the test exercises Read only the files that are actually referenced by the failures — do not read the entire tree speculatively.

tools.tool: read_file — to open specific test and production files
grep — to locate a class or method when the path is not obvious

step.title: Classify each failure
step.description: Assign exactly one root-cause label from this list: - assertion mismatch - NullPointerException - mock misconfiguration - missing stub - wrong exception type - timeout - other (explain in one sentence)

step.title: Group failures by root cause
step.description: If two or more failures share the same root cause, list them under one heading and write the explanation once. Reference the shared cause for subsequent tests: "Same root cause as ClassName.methodA above."

step.title: Produce the output
step.description: Write exactly three sections in order: Summary, Failures, Suggested Fixes. See output_format below.

hard_rules.rule: Plain text only — no ANSI escape codes, no markdown tables, no emoji.
Three labeled sections: Summary, Failures, Suggested Fixes.
Keep it short. One sentence beats two. A snippet beats a paragraph.
Snippets must be no more than ~10 lines. Omit boilerplate imports.

output_format.section: One to three sentences: how many tests failed, which classes, shared theme if any.

One entry per failure (or per group). Format:
[ClassName.methodName] - What failed: one sentence. - Root cause: label from the classification list. - Evidence: quote the key assertion or exception line from the report.

One fix block per failure (or per group). Format:
[ClassName.methodName] - Fix: one sentence describing the change. - Snippet: // short illustrative code here

root_cause_heuristics.heuristic: Expected vs actual values differ. Check what the production method actually returns vs what the test asserts. Common source: wrong test data or stale expectation after a production change.
A dependency was not injected or a mock returned null when the code expected an object. Check @InjectMocks wiring and that all collaborators are declared as @Mock fields.
when(...).thenReturn(...) was called on a real object, or the wrong overload was stubbed. Verify the argument matchers and that the mocked type matches the injected field type.

A method called during the test has no configured behavior, returning the Mockito default (null / 0 / false). Add a when(...).thenReturn(...) for every method the production code invokes on its mocks.

assertThatThrownBy or @Test(expected=...) specified a different exception class than what was thrown. Align the expectation with the actual exception or fix the production code to throw the right type.
The test exceeded its time limit. Check for blocking I/O, infinite loops, or a missing mock that caused a real network call.
